routing.ipv6RouteHelp:
Most proxies have no IPv6 at their exit.

A connection the proxy cannot carry dies right after it opens, and browsers never retry it over IPv4, so Google and YouTube fail to load.

When on, every proxy is checked once at its connection test. IPv6 is used only through a proxy that carries it; everything else goes over IPv4, unnoticed.

IPv6 always travels inside the VPN, never around it.

helpVpn.what: Hiddify adds a virtual network to your computer, and every app's internet traffic goes through it on its own: browsers, Telegram, games, updates and the rest. Nothing has to be set up in each app.
pros: Every app goes through Hiddify, with no settings in each app.
Apps that ignore proxy settings, such as Telegram and games, work too.
Name lookups (DNS) go through Hiddify as well, so sites blocked that way open too.
cons: The first time, your computer asks for administrator permission, to install Hiddify's background service. After that it connects without asking.
Turn off other VPN apps while you use it: two at once get in each other's way.

helpSystemProxy.what: Hiddify changes your computer's proxy setting. Apps that follow that setting, such as web browsers, send their traffic through Hiddify; the rest connect directly, as if Hiddify were off.
pros: Quick to turn on and off, and Hiddify puts the setting back when you disconnect.
Works next to other network tools on your computer.
cons: Apps that ignore the system proxy, such as Telegram, many games and some update tools, are not protected.
If they stop working, choose VPN mode instead.
